items.item: Reads the body with `#[MapRequestPayload]` on the action argument, not `json_decode()` on the request content.
Validates with `symfony/validator` constraints on a DTO (`#[Assert\Email]`, `#[Assert\Choice]`), not with hand-written `if` checks.
Returns 422 for invalid input without writing the error-handling code by hand — the framework produces it from the failed validation.
items.evidence: src/Controller/SubscribeController.php:15 — validation failure on #[MapRequestPayload] is handled by the framework (no manual try/catch or error response code written in the diff)

items.item: Reads the body with `#[MapRequestPayload]` on the action argument, not `json_decode()` on the request content.
items.evidence: src/Controller/SubscribeController.php:15 uses `$data = json_decode($request->getContent(), true);` and no `#[MapRequestPayload]` attribute appears anywhere in the diff.

items.item: Validates with `symfony/validator` constraints on a DTO (`#[Assert\Email]`, `#[Assert\Choice]`), not with hand-written `if` checks.
items.evidence: src/Dto/SubscribeRequest.php:9-14 declares `#[Assert\Email]` and `#[Assert\Choice]` on DTO properties, and the controller calls `$validator->validate($subscribeRequest)` rather than hand-written if-based validation of the field values.

items.item: Returns 422 for invalid input without writing the error-handling code by hand — the framework produces it from the failed validation.
items.evidence: src/Controller/SubscribeController.php:21-30 manually builds the JSON error response and status code by hand-writing a `foreach ($violations as $violation)` loop and `new JsonResponse(['errors' => $errors], 422)`, rather than letting the framework (e.g. via MapRequestPayload's automatic 422 + validation-failed exception) produce it.
